title: Toast the operator for waiting decisions and notable task changes, with a status-line count
description:
Operator instruction, first-party in the opum-doc session 2026-10-03, verbatim: "add toast alerts to the quest mode - when there are open decisions for me, status changes, etc. that I should be notified about". Design by opum-doc under constitution Article 5 clause 1 as amended: opum-doc docs/reference/quest-board-alerts-design.md (opum-ai/opum-doc#630, main 3d47205), relayed by opum-agent as seq 175 on OPAG-1089.

Alerts that toast, and for how long:
- a decision becomes `proposed` -- "DEC-140 needs a decision: (title)", 10 s, never batched;
- a `proposed` decision is resolved -- "DEC-140 decided: accepted", 6 s;
- a task moves to Paused -- "OPAG-777 paused in quest-cli: (title)", 8 s;
- a task moves to Closed -- "LCLI-660 closed (won't do) in lore-cli", 6 s;
- a HIGH-priority task moves to Done -- "OPAG-777 done: (title)", 6 s.
Everything else appears in the pane only and does not toast.

Batching: more than three alert-worthy changes in one check become one toast -- "5 updates: 3 done, 2 paused. Open /quest for the list." Decisions are never folded into a batch.

Status line: while any decision is `proposed`, a `$.ui.status` entry "Quest: 1 decision waiting", cleared when none are. A toast can be missed; the status line stays.

Polling: every 2 minutes whether or not the pane is open, since an alert matters most when the pane is closed. A task that leaves the open set gets ONE `quest task view`, to tell Done from Closed. The full board still refreshes only while the pane is visible.

No replays: the last state seen -- decision ids and statuses, open task ids and statuses -- is kept in `$.store`. The first check after install records a baseline and shows nothing. After a reload or restart the check compares against the stored state. Changes that happened while no session ran arrive as one summary toast, "While you were away: 1 decision waiting, 4 updates", plus the status-line count.

Quiet failure: a repository that cannot be read is skipped for that check and the board's existing "Could not read" line covers it. The check never toasts about its own read errors.

Setting: a `userConfig` option `alerts` -- `all` (default), `decisions` (decision toasts and the count only), `off`.

Heads-up recorded, not acted on: opum-doc is designing an operator-question record with the operator, which may change how "decisions waiting" is counted. Build to the design as it stands.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A new proposed decision toasts once and sets the status-line count, and resolving it toasts and clears the count
Paused, Closed and high-priority Done each toast, and a normal-priority Done does not
More than three alert-worthy changes in one check produce one batched toast, and decisions are never folded into it
Nothing toasts on the first, baseline check; a stored state suppresses repeats after a reload
the alerts userConfig offers all, decisions and off, and off produces no toast
The check runs every 2 minutes with the pane closed, and a task leaving the open set gets exactly one task view to tell Done from Closed
README read failure stays quiet: an unreadable repository produces no toast
